'''Mary Elizabeth Lynch Pillion''' (January 18, 1921 – June 8, 1990) was an American chemist with the United States Army from the late 1940s into the 1970s.

== Early life ==
Elizabeth Lynch was from [[Lawrence, Massachusetts]], the daughter of Michael Francis Lynch and Abigail F. Scott Lynch.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2005-08-11|title=Obituary for Michael Francis LYNCH (Aged 77)|pages=62|work=The Boston Globe|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/87491042/obituary-for-michael-francis-lynch/|access-date=2021-10-21|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

== Career ==
Pillion was a chemist at the [[United States Army]]'s [[Combat Capabilities Development Command Soldier Center|Quartermaster Research and Engineering Command]] in [[Natick, Massachusetts]]. Much of her work involved studying storage and cleaning methods for feeding and hydration systems in extreme environments. In 1962 she received the Research Directors' Award for her work on a [[Spectrophotometry|spectrophotometric]] correction technique for identifying ingredients in disinfectants and other solutions.<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=WaErAAAAYAAJ&pg=RA3-PA34 "QM R&E Command Selects 3 Employees for Awards Recognizing Achievement"] Army Research and Development Newsmagazine 3(April 1962): 34.</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=1962-02-18|title=Quartermasters Honor Engineer, Two Scientists|pages=56|work=The Boston Globe|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/87469819/quartermasters-honor-engineer-two/|access-date=2021-10-21|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

Pillion's research was published in scholarly journals including ''[[Analytical Chemistry (journal)|Analytical Chemistry]]'',<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Pillion|first1=Elizabeth.|last2=Rogers|first2=M. R.|last3=Kaplan|first3=A. M.|date=1961-11-01|title=Absorptivity Correction in Multicomponent Spectrophotometric Analysis|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ac60180a028|journal=Analytical Chemistry|volume=33|issue=12|pages=1715–1718|doi=10.1021/ac60180a028|issn=0003-2700|url-access=subscription}}</ref> ''[[Journal of Chromatographic Science]],''<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Pillion|first=Elizabeth|date=1965-07-01|title=Gas Chromatography of Phenylphenols and Chlorophenylphenols on a Silicone Nitrile Column|url=https://doi.org/10.1093/chromsci/3.7.238|journal=Journal of Chromatographic Science|volume=3|issue=7|pages=238–239|doi=10.1093/chromsci/3.7.238|issn=0021-9665|url-access=subscription}}</ref> ''[[Military Medicine (journal)|Military Medicine]]'',<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last1=Rogers|first1=Morris R.|last2=Vitaliano|first2=Joseph J.|last3=Kaplan|first3=Arthur M.|last4=Pillion|first4=Elizabeth|date=1977-04-01|title=Military Individual and Small Group Water Disinfecting Systems: An Assessment|url=https://doi.org/10.1093/milmed/142.4.268|journal=Military Medicine|volume=142|issue=4|pages=268–277|doi=10.1093/milmed/142.4.268|pmid=404587|issn=0026-4075|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and ''[[Applied and Environmental Microbiology|Applied Microbiology]]''.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last1=Kaplan|first1=Arthur M.|last2=Mandels|first2=Mary|last3=Pillion|first3=Elizabeth|last4=Greenberger|first4=Marvin|date=1970-07-01|title=Resistance of Weathered Cotton Cellulose to Cellulase Action|journal=Applied Microbiology|volume=20|issue=1|pages=85–93|doi=10.1128/am.20.1.85-93.1970|pmid=16349883|pmc=376872}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Elizabeth Lynch was married to John William Pillion, an Army physician. She lived in [[Andover, Massachusetts]]. She died in 1990, in [[Methuen, Massachusetts]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=1990-06-10|title=Elizabeth (Lynch) Pillion (death notice)|pages=87|work=The Boston Globe|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/87470281/elizabeth-lynch-pillion-death-notice/|access-date=2021-10-21|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>
